# 4 Maccabees Chapter 16 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Sinaiticus) | **Section:** The Mother's Speech Recalled

---

**1** If therefore a woman who was old and widowed in spirit, who had borne seven sons, endured to look on the torment of her children all the way to death, it must be acknowledged that devout reason is sovereign over the passions.

**2** I have thus demonstrated that not only men have exercised reason over the passions,

**3** but that even a woman despised the greatest sufferings. And the lions that surrounded Daniel were not so fierce, nor was the fiery furnace of Mishael so intensely hot,

**4** as the burning maternal desire she felt for her seven children; yet she watched them all die.

**5** With the reasoning that comes from religion, the mother quenched passions so great and so numerous.

**6** Consider also: if this woman, as a mother, had been weak in spirit, she would have mourned over them and perhaps spoken in some such manner:

**7** Alas for me and for my misery! I bore seven sons and now I am mother of none.

**8** O seven pregnancies all come to nothing! O seven months of labor and weariness, all in vain!

**9** Futile have been my nursings and bitter my sucklings; in vain, O sons, I suffered for you the many pains of childbirth,

**10** and still greater ones in your upbringing, and greatest of all in your agonizing deaths.

**11** Not one of my sons will close my eyes; not one will lay me in the tomb.

**12** But this blessed and holy woman, keeping her reasoning firm and unshaken, spoke not one such word.

**13** She did not weep or lament or say anything unworthy of herself; she did not yield to grief.

**14** Instead, she urged each of her sons forward to martyrdom for the sake of piety.

**15** O mother, faithful soldier of God! O venerable elder woman, valiant in battle! O woman stronger than all the men!

**16** You endured watching your children die for piety; you surrendered your whole family to God!

**17** Was it not you, O mother of those sons, who encouraged each one on his way to martyrdom and called out to each of them by name?

**18** You said to each: My son, do not flee from the contest; and through me you offered them as a burnt offering to God.

**19** O mother who surpassed all women in courage! O mother of seven children, most noble and most blessed!

**20** For what mother has ever watched seven sons die in a single day and been so filled with the spirit of devotion to God as to urge them all to die thus?

**21** You proved that reason is the sovereign master of the passions, O mother, through your holy sons.

**22** For these sons of yours swept out the ungodly Antiochus like a wind and a tide through the force of their reason and piety.

**23** For there are none like them, neither men nor women, anywhere in human memory who overcame the passions so completely.
